notes.title: Week 20: Patch 0.9.2 - Game Feature Complete 100% + My Next Roguelike Game
notes.notes:
[url=https://ibb.co/tDvLzW2][img]https://i.ibb.co/fHyD9PN/patch-notes-thumbnail-20.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Feature Complete[/h1]
The game is now technically 100% complete. Let's see what's left.

1) Remaining Plano Effects: These can wait a bit and be completed through the next patches.
2) Controller input: This can also wait a bit since there is no real demand for it, at least for now.
3) Localization: The publisher decided to push this after the full release so I predict late summer. 
4) Final Missions For Astral Link 5 levels: This will be added in the next patch, on May 20th.
5) Porting: The publisher will probably help with this after the full release so there is nothing to do for now.

So the game now offers the "final" experience. The full release date will be announced soon so the next patches should be light (some improvements and bug fixing here and there).

[h1]Accessible For New Players[/h1]
I kept trying to make the game even more accessible to new players throughout the last few patches since this has been a real problem even after fixing all the bugs and progression issues. Here is what I added this time:

1) Buying 5 booster packs at once now gives 1 extra, and buying 10 at once now gives 3 extra packs.
2) Mazais now only show up at Astral Link 3+ battles. Many people struggled with the Overdrive and Sacrifice mechanics so Mazais became overkill. 
3) All Astral Link 1 decks are now composed of the same Plano x20. This should make all the first battles a lot easier. 

[h1]Mission Complete[/h1]

The game isn't 100% done, there are still some patches left but the features are now 100% complete. I said the early access will last about 6 months and I think I managed to fix everything in time. No matter what happens moving forward, I want to thank all the people that helped me with feedback. 

I think the biggest game design mistake was the "Astral Link" feature. I wanted to do something different from other card games but it made the whole game a complicated mess. Unfortunately, I sinked too many too resources into it early on so I had to fully commit. The game will always have some flaws here and there but I hope that all these patches can at least make the overall experience enjoyable, especially for people who aren't too familiar with the game. 

[h1]Next Chapter - BLUE HUNTER[/h1]
[url=https://ibb.co/2MrPSqK][img]https://i.ibb.co/xgbGYh5/bh-1.png[/img][/url]

I have been working on Final Stardust since 2020 so it's been a long time. Starting your dream game as your first project is a really bad idea but I was willing to try everything I can to make it happen. Obviously, I had to pay a price for that. Therefore, I am thinking of taking a break after finishing "Cosmic Nexus". I will be working on a smaller project to test some ideas on the side and I plan to release the game this same year, on December 2024. If you are interested you can wishlist the game [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2992190/Blue_Hunter/]here[/url].

Alright, see you in 3-4 days.

notes.title: WEEK 18: PATCH 0.8.5 - PLAYER FEEDBACK QOLs & MISSIONS & TUTORIALS
notes.notes:
[url=https://ibb.co/GvVkDGL][img]https://i.ibb.co/SXK0gH8/patch-notes-thumbnail-18.png[/img][/url]

My initial plan was to add the Astral Link 5s and have the game be feature complete. However, I had tons of feedback from different reviews related to the fact that certain parts of the game are still not clear enough. 

I decided to delay the last Astral Links in favor of some QOLs that can improve the overall experience. I haven’t added everything yet but I have done so many changes so you should start to notice some difference. As usual, if there is a bug I will push a hotfix. Let’s talk about what’s added.

[h1]QOLs[/h1]

1) I had many complains about the UI, in terms of how unclear it is. I have replaced many arrows by a simple “close” button instead. All the UIs will be “closeable” via the ESC button once I start adding controller input, so it’ll be added this month.    

2) I added the first image tutorials to explain the main concepts. I will add one for the menu and one for the shop later to reveal some “not obvious” features. I will also update the rulebook with a “Supernova” section since that’s also unclear.

3) I have added a mission section to give a sort of purpose/goal to the player. You now know what you should do next. You will need to go through a battle to have the mission update to your current progress. Keep in mind that most of the missions require the maximum Astral Link level so it’s normal if you can’t access them yet this patch.

4) I added many details in battle to clarify certain parts. Some people got confused by EP/HP for example.

5) I added some “warning” texts here and there for non-obvious action results. For example, you might want to skip a tutorial but you are afraid of not being able to see it again. Speaking of that, I will add a section in the main menu to re-watch the image tutorials, like I did with the battle tutorial. 

Next patch will probably be 0.9.0. So this month will be all about finalizing the last touches to make the game provide a great experience. I can’t fix all the issues unfortunately but I will do what I can to fix the main issues at least. 

See you in the next patch!

[h1]Astral Link And Game Completion [/h1]

I added all the Astral Links level 4, no updated dialogue for now since it can wait. The only thing left is level 5, in the next patch, then the game is pretty much complete. 

[h1]Avatar Skins And Deck Variety[/h1]

You can now buy the starter decks you didn't choose in the shop. When you buy a starter pack you get a skin that comes with it. In fact, if you already have a save file the game should update your data and unlock your specific skin. For example, if you chose Jupiter you will have the Jupiter skin. You can change your skin by clicking on the skin icon in the explorer UI in the main menu. 

The Dark and Celestial skins should be unlocked in the next patch. I was thinking player level 20 gets you the Dark skin and unlocking your first Astral Link 5 gets you the Celestial skin. This way you can enjoy those skins while finishing the game. 

I have had many people complain about deck variety and struggling to access new cards. I did everything I can to make things easier, the starter decks should make things easier. The price was initially going to be 1k but I bumped it to 2k because it comes with a skin. An Astral Link level 1 battle gives you 100 gold and you need 2 wins to get to Astral Link 2, which gives you 200. This is besides all the gold you get as a bonus when you level up or unlock a new Astral Link level. 

This means that you can try a new element within 10 battles, I think it's good enough to try your existing element. Also, there is the welcome gift in the shop that allows to have 2k gold for free. I hope creating decks is now a lot more accessible. 

Alright, next patch, probably on May 1st will conclude this crazy journey and allow us to have a complete game.

notes.notes:

The Astral link system was huge so I had to delay the achievements to the next patch. The Astral link is the main progression in game. I will add a quick tutorial with images soon but for now let me explain.

[h1]ASTRAL LINK - MAIN PROGRESSION[/h1]

1) The '[b]Astral link[/b]' is a bond you have with a character in a location. Think of it as a friendship meter.
 
2) When you go to a location you have a best of 3 system. If you win twice in a row or if you win 2 battles out of 3 the Astral link increases. Then it's reset. Obviously, if you lose more than once nothing happens and you have to restart. The maximum Astral Link is 5. For now I only unlocked level 2 to do some testing, I will be unlocking a new level once per week. 

3) When the Astral link increases [b]MANY THINGS[/b] change:
a/ The dialogue (to make it feel like the character is affected by your actions).

b/ The Elementalist deck. If you check the deck viewer on the left you will notice that some cards are different.

c/ Your fastest time against that Elementalist changes based on the Astral link level. If it's level 1, the best time for level 1 is displayed. If it's level 2, the best time for level 2 is displayed (I forgot to add the code to update the values but it's added to the save system).

c/ The highest battle score (new) is displayed. Same thing as time.

d/ You can move from one Astral Link to another at any time. For example, if you unlocked level 2 but you want to go back to level 1 to improve your score you can do that. 

e/ The story. There is no real story but all the dialogues add a sort of a story and finishing the game will require reaching level 5 with a couple of Elementalists. This will be more obvious in the achievements.

f/ Dark cards. Besides level up, there is no other way to obtain the strongest Dark cards (not in the shop) since they can't be crafted. So I am thinking that the best of 3 in level 5 should give a random Dark card. Basically when you are level 5 the best of 3 system becomes useless since you can't go beyond that. What if it made you unlock Dark cards instead?

g/ The amount of gold stardust and blue stardust increase. The equation is very simple. Amount = base * level. For example, level 3 = 100 gold * 3 = 300 gold stardust.

i/ The experience you get per battle increases. However, I am stupid again, I forgot to add it in this patch so it'll be added in the next one.

If each Elementalist has 5 decks that's 105 decks overall. As for dialogue lines, it'll be 500+ in total. Overall, you can see how impactful the Astral Link system is and why the progression was really bad at launch. Special thanks to Rayze and Whack on Discord for helping me to create decks for different Astral Link levels. 

[h1]PLAYER FEEDBACK - GOLD GIFT[/h1]
 
Someone mentioned that getting cards is very hard at the beginning. I completely understand. If the Astral link stays at 1, farming gold and xp takes forever. I added a free gift in the shop so that you get 4 booster packs of your choice. I hope that helps. Once all the Astral Links are unlocked things will get better since 1 win = 1 booster pack. 

The idea is having a slow start but making grinding in the later stages a lot easier. 

[h1]QUICK START - LOADING TIMES[/h1]

I made some optimizations and you will notice the game starts very quickly now which is cool. However, the trade-off is that scene loading takes a bit more time. For example, going into battles will take a couple of extra seconds. Just wanted to mention it.

[h1]BATTLE TIME[/h1]

I increased the MG in battles to 6k. 4k is perfect for the 5 mins battle length, however, if you have very strong cards you can demolish Astral link 1 levels very easily, making battles extremely short. I want to see if battles get longer now but if they are too long I will bring it back to 4k. 

[h1]CONCLUSION[/h1]

We moved to version 0.8.0 now and next month will be 0.9.X. We are getting close to the full release. Pretty much all the features are implemented now so it's all about adding the small details (finishing Dark overdrive effects, adding avatar skins, adding the remaining Astral links, etc...). I am not including controller input and localization.

Yes, I was greedy as usual haha, hence the delay. This is a BIG update because I decided to add new battle modes on top of adding tons of overdrive effects.

The current mode is now called "Supersonic". This is a very fast paced format made for digital games. 
The first new mode is called "Paragon". This is a slower format, made for a TCG format.
The second new mode is called "Apeiron". This is a very simplistic and very slow format. This is for people who want old school mechanics.

The great thing about this is that you can use the different modes to slowly learn how to play the game. Apeiron > Paragon > Supersonic. We are just missing a rulebook now and it'll be perfect.

I noticed the Supersonic mode was dumping too much info at once so I hope these new modes will make the learning curve smoother. Apeiron for example doesn't have Mazai/Overdrive effects and attacks only work if your Plano's EP is higher than the rival's EP.

[h1]Effects[/h1]
I have added so many new effects so bugs might happen. Thanks for those always sending feedback for that.

I haven't added all the Plano effects yet but one thing I started to realize is how big the game is getting especially for a solo dev. The effects are going towards 400+
and I am definitely starting to feel the technical debt (the game was never meant to go this far). 

There are 100 Planos, so 100 effects. Each Plano has an overdrive effect. So 200 effects overall. Each Plano has a Dark form so an extra 100 effects (coming soon).
Each Dark Plano has an overdrive too (coming soon) so it'll add another 100. Overall, we have 400 effects. This is without mentioning the 20 Mazai effects that are now complete.

I hope all of this gives tons of deckbuilding options, especially with Regular & Dark Planos having cross-compatible evolutions.

I will give more details about the battle modes later, for now have fun testing things and see how they work.

[h1]TCG Ideas/Discussion[/h1]

Balancing will always be done around the Supersonic format to keep battles dynamic.

In a paper/TCG format, I think all the values being divided by 100 will simplify all the battle calculations. Another concern in a TCG is calculating the HP/EP for each

As for the space counter resource I would expect it to be some extra cards that you have as an extra deck. Then you put them below your field and each turn you add a new card there. To consume a space counter you just rotate the card to the side and at the end of the turn it goes back to normal. 

We are still far from having anything physical but it was fun testing some new ideas.

It's worth mentioning that some Plano effect can be obsolete in certain battle modes. For example those that are involved with residual space counters. 
So the utility of a card can vary depending on the battle mode. Not only these battles modes will add more game content but they will also give you a reason
to utilize more deck slots in the deckbuilding UI. I might bring back the 9 space counters to the Paragon and Apeiron modes though because residual space counters don't work.

I am glad to say that I found a publisher (Freedom games) to help me with console releases. I can talk more about this in the future, let's go back to the game itself for now.

Now I want to cover some features we can implement in the future. Let's discuss!

[h1]1) NEW BATTLE MODE?[/h1]

Since I slowed down the patch release pace a bit I started with some clean up in the project and I added a couple of changes to the cards to make them more "understandable".

I am also planning on adding a new game mode that is based on a TCG format. I think for a digital game it's better to have very dynamic battles, however, TCGs are a different story.

Since I would like to experiment with a TCG someday, I think it'll be cool to add a game mode now that we can experiment with. The TCG format should still keep the "simple" aspect of the game while making battles a bit longer. I think this is also a good way to add more content since every battle can be played in 2 different ways.

The only problem with this is the game wasn't conceived with other game modes in mind so there might be some bugs and changes will happen over a couple of patches. The most
tricky part is definitely the Plano effect descriptions.

For now here is the concept I have:

a) New win condition. Turns will start at 40 instead of 16 and if you don't have any card left to draw you lose.
b) Each player will have his own Vortex (previously Black hole)?.
c) Only one card is drawn each turn instead of 5.
d) Cards in hand don't go to the Vortex (previously Black hole) at the end of the turn.
e) MG increased to 8000?.
f) All stats and effect numbers are divided by 100 for easier calculations? For example a 2200 HP will be 22 HP only. 500 effect damage will become 5 damage only. 
The MG will be 80 instead of 8000. I am not sure about this one. 
g) Disable residual space counters? A bit tricky since some Planos have effects related to it.

Let me know if you have some extra ideas.

[h1]2) STORY MODE?[/h1]
So it seems like many people are interested in a Story mode but I am still not sure about this one. This is why I would like to get more feedback about it.

Here are a couple of problems:

a) I don't want to spend time on a story only for people to skip all the dialogue.
b) The story won't be as good as the manga version and will have an alternative ending that's more adapted to a video game.
c) Late release. This is definitely my mistake. However, if I release a story and the difficulty slowly increases with it most people will find it boring
because they already have maxed out decks before playing it. The only way I can see this working is if the story mode is after the Astral link mode (winning against
all the characters in the map) and will have maxed out difficulty (very strong decks) from the start. 
d) Player freedom. Initially I wanted to have characters unlock one by one but I think that's a bit limiting in terms of what you can do. It might be more interesting to have all the characters
unlocked at once and you choose your own way of making progress (especially once there is actual progression). This is especially true for a game without a story mode (at least for now).

This is why I am hesitating a bit with a story mode. If you have other ideas for the story let me know. I want to make sure I spend my time on features that people want.

Now we have everything we need for a GOOD tutorial. Sorry for the delay. I kept changing mechanics over and over that it wasn't worth it to make a tutorial.

The new plano sacrifice mechanic allows you to sacrifice a Plano and transfer his effect to the selected Plano. It works exactly like an evolution.
If the game detects that the selected Plano isn't the right one for an evolution it'll default to sacrifice. The easiest way to get it is to give it a try.

This is huge in terms of gameplay since it means that you can play any card at any point (as long as you have enough space counters).

3) If you evolve you get benefits (no timeout + overdrive if in Eclispe slot).
4) You can sacrifice a Plano in your hand to use him as a spell by selecting an existing Plano.

[h1]NEW DIRECTION[/h1]
Not even 2 months in and the battle system is a different beast already. The new Steam trailer will be postponed until some of the new mechanics are added so it can reflect the actual state of the game (since the game changed a lot from release). I tested so many mechanics since launch so it was chaos for a while. However, I think that now I have a clear vision for my what I want and all the future changes will go in the same direction. 

First, all the card types will be removed, and only Plano cards will remain (a small exception with Mazais). Cards like Saiments for example have effects that can be triggered by Planos themselves. I also think that focusing on Planos only will force me to come up with more interesting/original mechanics. The more you play Final Stardust the more you will realize it's just a monster taming game but with cards. Since there is a limited card pool (100 Planos + 100 variants) most of the focus will be placed on mechanics. I think the game will become even simpler but you will have more "playstyle" options overall. More on that below. 

To keep the casual approach, my final goal is to reach a point where the player does nothing but place Planos and let the magic happen. It might seem like it's going to be more boring that way but the game flow will improve drastically. Don't listen to me, just give it a try.

[h1]IN-BATTLE TUTORIAL[/h1]
With all the stuff that I talk about, I can understand how most people can be confused (especially if you don't read any of these posts or aren't in the Discord). This is why I will slow down the work on mechanics and work on an in-battle tutorial for the next patch. Even if not all the mechanics are present, I think the basics should be enough to get people going.

[h1]UPDATE [/h1]
Upon loading, your Saiments and Mazai cards will be automatically deleted and replaced by Gold Stardust plus Blue Stardust. In the next patch I will remove Spells and Eishougis. All the Planos are now available in game and crafting was added. Celestial Planos can only be obtainable via crafting. Dark variants of Celestial Planos will be unlocked later via the Astral Link levels. Keep in that mind that not all Planos have an effect yet, especially with the Overdrive.

[h1]FIRST MECHANIC[/h1]
The new mechanic that was implemented this time was the "Random" field effects. The previous Mazai cards were a bit useless most of the time, so I decided to rework the whole mechanic. Now, each battle will have random field effects that will activate after a certain number of turns. The number of turns are also random (either 3, 6, or 9 but the positioning is random). These Mazai cards can't be collected, they are only present in battle. Since I just added the mechanic, there are only 3 Mazais that rotate. Penetrating the enemy defense is usually the most difficult part, and this will become more apparent when Spells and Eishougis will be removed. Therefore, I added Mazais that destroy Planos. I tried to prioritize the losing player in terms of conditions to always favor comebacks.

Mazai effects happen at the end of the turn. I am not sure I want to have "continuous" effects that work all the time since I think it'll add a good amount of complexity and interfere with the "simple" design I am going for. In case it's not clear, Mazai effects work in lanes (all the Planos on the left, all the Planos in the middle or all the Planos on the right).

[h1]NEXT MECHANICS[/h1]
These are the next mechanics that will be implemented.

1) Random slots. The overdrive effects are triggered when a Plano is summoned in the middle slot and it usually impacts the side Planos. However, I am thinking of randomizing slot positions at the beginning of the battle, like I did with Mazais. So when an overdrive triggers it'll specify a "type" of slot to impact and that slot can be in any position. I know it's confusing so I think it's better to wait until you see it in action.
2) Another idea is to use Planos as Spells. If you use a Plano that doesn't work as an evolution, it gets detected as a Spell instead and it just triggers its effect on the slot. This means you sacrifice a Plano in your hand to impact a Plano on the field (triggering the effect of the sacrificed Plano, for example). Just an idea for now.
3) With Mazai effects having such an important role now, I might add the option to attack them too (to counter their effects).
4) Elemental skills. This will be similar to the Yu-Gi-Oh Duel Links skills and it'll be a specific effect that triggers at the beginning of the battle. This can help with diversity especially when the different AI Astral Link levels are enabled.

[h1]NEW QUOTE[/h1]
In the future, the main quote will change to "Choose your element(s)". After a lot of experimentation, I realized Final Stardust will be about combining elements and not just picking one. This will be more and more obvious when all the Plano effects are implemented.

[h1]90% Discount[/h1]
Before I say anything, I just started a 90% discount (2 weeks) so the game is almost free. If you didn't get the game yet this is best time to do it!

[h1]Manga[/h1]
The second chapter of the manga will be coming soon, probably within the next few weeks.

[h1]Hotfix[/h1]
This patch was initially a hotfix but I took 2 more days to add a couple of things with it. The problems that were mentioned a couple of days ago should be fixed now. 

[h1]Exhaust[/h1]
Instead of limiting cards with a number of copies in the deck, I will only add an Exhaust mechanic for now. This means very strong cards can't be re-shuffled into the deck. Nerfing the values plus adding an exhaust should be enough for most cards. The maximum amount of exhausted cards in the black hole is 10, beyond that it doesn't do anything (who knows maybe someone wants a full deck of cards that exhaust). Needless to say, when cards are exhausted they don't contribute to Plano effects that involve the black hole.

[h1]New Trailer[/h1]
I will update the trailer and the description to delay the avatar creation. I think most people so far agreed that gameplay is king and keeping the current Steam page is a bit confusing for newcomers. Even though I haven't followed the exact path I wanted with the patches (following feedback) the game has improved a lot since release so it was the right choice. I will upload the new video tomorrow. 

[h1]Card Limitation[/h1]
There won't be any specific limitations when it comes to elements. The other deck slots will be unlocked within the upcoming patches and it'll still be possible to mix different elements. Effects and enemy AIs will be built around elements but the player will be able to choose whatever he wants, to increase the number of possible decks since the total number of cards is limited.

[h1]Spell Rework[/h1]
I don't know when exactly since this will take a good amount of work but Spells, Eishougis and Saiments will all be reworked and belong to only one group: "Spell". Eishougis are just AOE spells and Saiments are technically utility based spells. For this reason, and to simplify things for future players, the Eishougi and Saiment types will be removed from the game. Even the Saiment icons will be changed to something similar to the current spells (for more visual consistency). Saiments will only be used in the manga to represent actual cards since spells aren't cards in the story (imagine a fireball). 

[h1]Mazai Rework[/h1]
While tweaking the Mazai effects I realized that I was very limited in terms of what I can do with them. This is based on their concept (a field effect) and the philosophy of "only one sentence effects". A lot of effects were repeated versions of Plano effects. So I might either remove them or rework them in a different way. 

If you check out some old Final Stardust footage you will find something I tested called "Turn effects". After X amount of turns a random effect happens. This is to add RNG in battle and make each battle feel unique. I tried some randomness with Planos but it wasn't great, however, it might work with Mazai cards. 

I also noticed that Marvel Snap had something similar with their location system. 3 random locations in battle and each one of them has a unique effect. With 20 unique Mazais in game, if each battle has 3 random Mazais that trigger a certain effect after X amount of turns it'll add even more replayability (swap Planos on the right lane, destroy Planos in the middle lane, double the EP of Planos on the left lane, etc...). I think it's worth a shot. 

[h1]Effect Philosophy[/h1]
Final Stardust's effects are supposed to be simple so that anyone can come in and start playing. Made by a casual...for casuals. The game depth lies in the layers: Mazai effect > Plano effect > Overdrive. So one effect is simple by itself but you can do combos by stacking different effects. At least that's my idea for now. After the "Spell rework" there should only be 3 types of cards in the game (Planos, Mazais & Spells) which should makes things more straightforward. The term "Plavolution" will also revert back to just "evolution". 

A lot of effects are "placeholder" to unlock new cards. So more interesting effects might be introduced in the future. It's better to build the foundation now before committing to progression with the Astral Link levels.

notes.title: WEEK 6: PATCH 0.6.4 - BATTLE SYSTEM V3 (BIG UPDATE)
notes.notes:
[url=https://ibb.co/JK24xdS][img]https://i.ibb.co/9N2Lwvd/patch-notes-thumbnail-6.png[/img][/url]

Okay, this is the biggest patch so far. It might not appear like that because all the effect changes are expressed in one line and all the changes are logic based. 
The battle system should feel different now as we are getting closer to the final version (thinking about adding a tutorial soon).
 
Since I introduced so many new effects (Normal effects, Overdrive, Mazai, etc...) in such a short period of time I probably broke the game with some of the effects. I know some of the Mazai effects might be broken because I am in the middle of changing them.

I don't do a lot of testing for now to keep patches dynamic. I will work on quick hotfixes whenever needed and the next patch will be in the next 2-3 days anyway (to add the features that I couldn't add in time).

[h1]Positioning[/h1]

Even though I am creating a sort of "Yu-Gi-Oh for casuals" game, I still want the game to have a sort of unique mechanic. This is why I am doubling down on positioning. I recommend checking all the new effects in the card collection UI. For now only 74/100 Planos have new effects and only 27 of them (mainly Venus) have an overdrive effect. Keep in mind that Planos from the same line usually have the same effect but the effect gets stronger with each new stage. The strongest Planos will be unlocked in the next patch.

[list]
[*] All Plano effects that impact an enemy Plano are changed to mono target. To be more specific, the effects only impact the opposing/facing Plano. This means that you need to position yourself in front of an enemy Plano if you want to affect it. So it's not just about triggering effects but also about positioning yourself.

[*] Overdrive effects only work on Planos in your own field. They usually impact the right or left Plano. This also contributes into thinking more about positioning. It also makes a lot of useless/weak cards more viable. 

[*] Another reason why I don't add Plano effects that you can activate later. You have to think about where to place the Plano. Place it in the wrong slot and you lose the effect. If you can activate it later there is no punishment. I am also not sure "continuous" effects are necessary because you always draw new cards each turn so you don't run out of actions to do.

[*] I think many Yu-Gi-Oh like effects might not be convenient in the game. For example returning a card to the hand (since hand cards are discarded and re-shuffled) or switching slots (hard to balance). Making other slots overdrive too can be too OP. I will definitely need more testing/feedback for this.
[/list]

[h1]Streamlining[/h1]

Another thing I am focusing on is making the battles streamlined. Let me explain.

[list]
[*] Since effects only affect the opposing Plano there is no more selection to do. This will make the battles flow better. Only non-Plano cards will have a selection possible (Saiments/Spells).

[*] This is already done but it's the same thing with attacks. Each Plano automatically attacks the one facing him that way there is no selection needed.

[*] Plano effects can't target multiple Planos at once anymore. Multi target is only for Mazai effects now. The only exception is some very strong Planos.

[*] Making the game play a bit like chess. Chess by itself is boring so it's about getting the good parts out of it. If you are a casual you can just steamroll through the game and just have fun. And for people who are more comfortable they can have more depth and think about different strategies they can implement.

[*] I am trying to get battles into the 5-10 mins mark. That way it's dynamic enough and it doesn't drag on for too long.

[*] Having a secondary effect (overdrive) might feel a bit clunky at first but it only triggers if a Plano is summoned in the middle and I think overall the pros outweigh the cons.

[*] The goal is to have the least amount of steps possible to do for each action. I only played a couple of battles in "Marvel Snap" but I liked how the emphasis was on positioning. For this reason "revive" like effects might be reworked in the future.

[*] Thinking about keeping the stats after a Plavolution, I am not sure keeping the status effect is good idea. I think keeping the same status effects will slow the pace down a lot. The main advantage of the Plavolution is not having a timeout effect. Unless I make it so that you keep the status effect until it's a timeout. Timeout is made as a status effect to be countered by other effects.
[/list]

[h1]Content[/h1]
[list]
[*] I unlocked some cards in the booster packs and everything will be available when I add crafting (next patch). All the cards in the game will be playable (even if some effects can change in the future). This way people have something to do while I focus on adding progression to the game.

[*] One last feature that can be worth adding later is "Elemental skills". Something like Yu-Gi-Oh Duel Links' skills where you can choose a special effect that gets triggered at the start of the battle. I will only add this when all the battle mechanics are implemented.

[*] I also have 5 dark and 5 celestial Mazai concept arts. I am still not sure if I should add them because I don't know if their effects can be balanced.
[/list]

[h1]Comebacks[/h1]
One important thing I want to have in battles is the ability to comeback from a losing position. There is nothing worse than knowing you already lost and just stalling the game. This is one of the reasons I added the "drawing 5 new cards" each turn. Drawing one cards each turn isn't enough for that. Therefore, all Plano effects that involve the black hole affect both the player and the enemy Planos. This means you can revive the enemy's Plano even if you don't have it. This should make it easier to comeback. 


[h1]Playstyles[/h1]
To remind everyone of the goal with elements/playstyle. Dark and Celestial aren't playstyles, they just add on top of the existing elements.
[list]
[*] Venus needs to be the tanky playstyle that's hard to kill.
[*] Mercury is the obnoxious playstyle that spams status effects.
[*] Jupiter is an "agile" playstyle that allows you to do a lot of unique/cool things. 
[*] Mars is the high damage playstyle that piercies through everything.
[/list]

[h1]Status effects[/h1]
It's worth talking about status effects. Some effects aren't applied directly but via status effects. This way they can be countered as well.
I don't know where exactly I should specify their explanations but for now you can find the explanation on the status Saiments themselves.

If a Plano already has a status effect nothing happens. In the future I might make it so that the new status effect overwrites the existing one. This not only adds more strategy but it fixes the problem of your effect being nullified because the opposing Plano already has a timeout.

[h1]Next Effects[/h1]
I won't mention balancing because that's a given but having unique effects for Dark Planos is something that will be added too. Dark Planos having "opposite" effects to the normal Planos. You can already Plavolve in both ways (from normal to dark and vice versa). All of this should add more variety/possibilities once deck rules are added (for example being mono element instead of mixing elements). 

Keep in mind that Final Stardust's quote is "Choose your element". So the final goal is to make people excited about choosing a specific element. That being said, you will be able to craft different decks of different elements once I add deck slots. I am also of thinking of adding "element" levels (getting xp for using a specific deck). Dark and Celestial Planos can be used in any deck as they are "secondary" elements.

[h1]Goal[/h1]
While the previous patch greatly improved the resource management in battle, it introduced another problem: Using all your cards at once. 

To tackle this I thought about two solutions: 
1) Each turn you continue to draw until you have 5 cards in your hand (like in Yu-Gi-Oh Rush Duel). However, I noticed some instances where I had strong cards and I couldn't do much. 
2) Draw 5 new cards each turn. This one adds another dimension to the battle while also making everything more dynamic (you always have cards to play). This mechanic is similar to what "Slay The Spire" does. 

I plan to keep patches short (every 2-3 days) that way the community can contribute a bit more by giving quick feedback. I am confident we can make the battle system a lot more fun within the next few weeks, then we can start adding more content.

notes.title: PATCH 0.5.2 (BATTLE SYSTEM GAMEPLAY UPDATE)
notes.notes:
I know some people are pissed because the avatar creation isn't available yet while it's showcased on the page but I will be adding that soon. 

However, before doing that I wanted to overhaul the battle system's resource system to make the gameplay a bit more fun, that way it's easier for people to wait. I have been trying to find the "Final Stardust" formula so I tested a bunch of stuff but that led to very boring gameplay sessions because the whole battle system was a mess. 

I made all the cards focus on space counters so now it'll be a lot more dynamic. 

I tweaked the elemental calculation as well. If it's not good I will completely remove it. 

I might even remove evolutions and make all monsters "summonable" with just space counters. We will see. Some people asked about evolutions so I added a collection UI in the menu to see all the monsters. You can even check those that aren't implemented yet. 

I got a lot of feedback on Discord and that helped me to know what to prioritize.
